x: A few weeks later, in the Walton A.C. promotion, Wally Ives was 3rd in 55.32, R. Rolfe 11th and R.
Our remaining walkers, Alan Robins, Syd Spencer and Gordon Doubleday, all finished the course, whilst Ron Fairman was obliged to retire with blistered feet.

It was pleasing to see young Joe Scamell walking so well again and hope this will continue during the track season. The handicap was deservedly won by Eric Hall (1.30) with Ron Fairman(16.00), 2nd, and Hugh McGreechan (0.40) 3rd.
Doubleday 9th (89.29) and Ron Garwood 12th (91.15) made up our team with a score of 24 points to Surrey W.C.'s 26. Joe Wilson, George Beecham, Albert Skinner, another new member, and R.

George Beecham walked an excellent first Brighton to gain a first class standard and Rolfe, Doub, and Joe Wilson gained 2nd class standards, as also did Alf Joels who was in the "B" Team. Ron Fairman failed to finish the course so our "B" team did not close in.
The handicap was won by Eric Hall with Evergreen Bob Readman 2nd, and Doub and Ron Fairman tying for third place. The match resulted in a win for us by 235 points to 295.

At Croydon Norman Guilmant was 4thm George Beecham, very fit after his holiday 5th, Hugh McGreechan 7th, Harry Shields 20th and Bernard 23rd, with Fred Rolfe, Bert Stallardm Ron Fairman, Joe Wilson and George Oliver coming along behind.
